questions.prompt: A covered audit team member directly owns $300 of the client’s common stock. What is the most appropriate independence conclusion?

choices.text: Independence is impaired despite the small amount.
Independence is preserved because the investment is immaterial.
Only disclosure to the audit committee is necessary.
Independence is impaired only if dividends are received.

questions.explanation: A covered member’s direct financial interest is prohibited. Neither a small balance, disclosure, nor the absence of dividends removes the interest.

questions.prompt: A nonissuer asks its auditor to approve all vendor payments during a controller vacancy. Which response is appropriate?

choices.text: Accept if the audit partner later reviews the payments.
Decline to authorize transactions because that is a management responsibility.
Accept because the vacancy is temporary.
Accept if the client signs a waiver.

questions.explanation: Authorizing transactions is management participation. A subsequent review, temporary arrangement, or waiver does not make the auditor independent.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes independence in appearance?

choices.text: The auditor personally believes no bias exists.
The audit firm has never received a client complaint.
A reasonable, informed third party would view the auditor as able to act objectively.
Every team member uses identical professional judgments.

questions.explanation: Appearance evaluates the informed third party’s perspective. Personal confidence is independence of mind and is not sufficient by itself.

questions.prompt: An audit senior proposes uploading identifiable client payroll to an unapproved public AI service. The client engagement letter is silent. What should happen first?

choices.text: Upload because the tool promises an accurate answer.
Upload after replacing only the company’s name.
Upload because all professional tools are covered by the audit opinion.
Evaluate confidentiality and authorization requirements before sending the data.

questions.explanation: Professional confidentiality applies to automated third-party tools. Accuracy, superficial anonymization, and the existence of an engagement do not establish authorization or adequate protection.

questions.prompt: A situation is expressly prohibited by an applicable independence rule. Can the conceptual framework authorize it after safeguards are documented?

choices.text: No; a framework cannot override an express prohibition.
Yes, if two partners approve the safeguards.
Yes, if the client is privately held.
Only if the prohibited service is inexpensive.

questions.explanation: The framework addresses threats when the rules permit an evaluation. It is not an exception to a direct prohibition.

questions.prompt: A firm audits an issuer and proposes a service permitted under an AICPA nonissuer interpretation. What additional evaluation is required?

choices.text: No evaluation because AICPA permissions control every audit.
Apply the relevant SEC and PCAOB restrictions and audit-committee requirements.
Only evaluate whether fees exceed audit fees.
Only confirm that the engagement partner is a CPA.

questions.explanation: Issuer engagements can be subject to additional or more restrictive independence requirements; nonissuer permissions are not portable without analysis.

questions.prompt: You are the ethics reviewer for a firm considering four proposed arrangements for a nonissuer financial-statement audit. Determine the appropriate conclusion for each fact pattern. Proposed arrangements: A: The engagement partner directly owns 20 client shares. B: The firm will prepare a proposed depreciation schedule; a competent controller chooses methods and accepts responsibility. C: An auditor will sign purchase orders for the client. D: Confidential customer data will be sent to a public tool without authorization. Evaluation instructions: Assume all individuals described are covered members. No exception applies to direct interests or management responsibilities. For permitted nonattest assistance, management must oversee, evaluate, and accept the results. Required: Arrangement A: appropriate conclusion.

choices.text: Permitted because shares are immaterial
Permitted with client consent
Prohibited direct financial interest
Management responsibility

questions.explanation: A covered partner’s direct interest impairs independence.

questions.prompt: You are the ethics reviewer for a firm considering four proposed arrangements for a nonissuer financial-statement audit. Determine the appropriate conclusion for each fact pattern. Proposed arrangements: A: The engagement partner directly owns 20 client shares. B: The firm will prepare a proposed depreciation schedule; a competent controller chooses methods and accepts responsibility. C: An auditor will sign purchase orders for the client. D: Confidential customer data will be sent to a public tool without authorization. Evaluation instructions: Assume all individuals described are covered members. No exception applies to direct interests or management responsibilities. For permitted nonattest assistance, management must oversee, evaluate, and accept the results. Required: Arrangement B: appropriate conclusion.

choices.text: Automatically prohibited for every nonissuer
No professional responsibilities apply
Client waiver substitutes for oversight
Evaluate and document nonattest safeguards

questions.explanation: Management retains responsibility, so evaluate the service and applicable safeguards.

questions.prompt: You are the ethics reviewer for a firm considering four proposed arrangements for a nonissuer financial-statement audit. Determine the appropriate conclusion for each fact pattern. Proposed arrangements: A: The engagement partner directly owns 20 client shares. B: The firm will prepare a proposed depreciation schedule; a competent controller chooses methods and accepts responsibility. C: An auditor will sign purchase orders for the client. D: Confidential customer data will be sent to a public tool without authorization. Evaluation instructions: Assume all individuals described are covered members. No exception applies to direct interests or management responsibilities. For permitted nonattest assistance, management must oversee, evaluate, and accept the results. Required: Arrangement C: primary issue.

choices.text: Assuming management responsibility
Only an immaterial financial interest
No independence issue
A required audit procedure

questions.explanation: Signing purchase orders authorizes client transactions.

questions.prompt: You are the ethics reviewer for a firm considering four proposed arrangements for a nonissuer financial-statement audit. Determine the appropriate conclusion for each fact pattern. Proposed arrangements: A: The engagement partner directly owns 20 client shares. B: The firm will prepare a proposed depreciation schedule; a competent controller chooses methods and accepts responsibility. C: An auditor will sign purchase orders for the client. D: Confidential customer data will be sent to a public tool without authorization. Evaluation instructions: Assume all individuals described are covered members. No exception applies to direct interests or management responsibilities. For permitted nonattest assistance, management must oversee, evaluate, and accept the results. Required: Arrangement D: required first action.

choices.text: Upload because the data is useful
Resolve authorization and confidentiality protections
Obtain only the tool’s accuracy score
Delay documentation until after upload

questions.explanation: Confidentiality duties apply before sharing client data with a third party.

questions.prompt: An auditor accepts management’s explanation despite contradictory shipping documents because the CFO has always been honest. Which concern is most direct?

choices.text: Excessive substantive testing.
Insufficient professional skepticism.
A prohibited audit opinion on a profitable client.
A need to assume all management statements are fraudulent.

questions.explanation: Past honesty does not resolve current inconsistent evidence. Skepticism requires follow-up without automatically assuming dishonesty.

questions.prompt: Who is responsible for preparing the financial statements and maintaining relevant internal control?

choices.text: The external auditor alone.
The auditor’s specialist.
Management.
The external confirmation respondent.

questions.explanation: Management owns financial reporting and control responsibilities. The external auditor evaluates and reports rather than assuming those duties.

questions.prompt: Which description of a financial-statement audit is most accurate?

choices.text: It guarantees that all fraud has been detected.
It guarantees that the entity will remain solvent.
It certifies that every transaction is correct.
It provides reasonable assurance about material misstatement of the statements as a whole.

questions.explanation: An audit provides high, not absolute, assurance and focuses on material misstatement, not a guarantee of transaction accuracy or business success.

questions.prompt: A team searches only for evidence supporting its initial conclusion that a reserve is adequate. Which bias is most apparent?

choices.text: Confirmation bias.
An unavoidable legal prohibition.
Random sampling risk.
A required use of management representations.

questions.explanation: Selective support for an initial conclusion is confirmation bias. Consider alternative assumptions and contradictory evidence.

questions.prompt: A company has strong approval controls, but its CEO can post unrestricted top-side entries. What is the appropriate response?

choices.text: Conclude fraud risk is eliminated by the approvals.
Assess and respond to management-override risk.
Ignore entries if the company is profitable.
Replace all substantive procedures with the CEO’s written representation.

questions.explanation: Management may bypass ordinary controls. The auditor must address override, including relevant entries and unusual transactions.

questions.prompt: An auditor identifies evidence that the CEO may have intentionally misstated revenue. Whom should the auditor consider communicating with directly?

choices.text: Only the employee who entered the transaction.
Only customers who bought the product.
Those charged with governance at an appropriate level.
No one until the auditor can guarantee fraud occurred.

questions.explanation: The level of implicated management affects escalation. Appropriate governance communication is not conditioned on proving every element of a legal fraud claim.

questions.prompt: Review four statements from the engagement file and identify the best corrective action. File excerpts: 1. The CFO was reliable last year, so contrary evidence was disregarded. 2. The team has promised investors that the company will never fail. 3. A senior selected only documents supporting the original reserve. 4. The CEO can override normal journal approval. Required approach: Base the audit on sufficient appropriate evidence, maintain a questioning mind, distinguish audit assurance from investment guarantees, and address management override. Required: Correct the treatment of contrary evidence.

choices.text: Rely on past honesty
Ignore nonfinancial records
Assume fraud without further work
Investigate and resolve the inconsistency

questions.explanation: Skepticism requires investigating the inconsistent evidence.

questions.prompt: Review four statements from the engagement file and identify the best corrective action. File excerpts: 1. The CFO was reliable last year, so contrary evidence was disregarded. 2. The team has promised investors that the company will never fail. 3. A senior selected only documents supporting the original reserve. 4. The CEO can override normal journal approval. Required approach: Base the audit on sufficient appropriate evidence, maintain a questioning mind, distinguish audit assurance from investment guarantees, and address management override. Required: Correct the assurance promise.

choices.text: Explain reasonable assurance about material misstatement
Guarantee solvency
Guarantee every transaction
Withdraw all audit objectives

questions.explanation: The audit does not guarantee business success.

questions.prompt: Review four statements from the engagement file and identify the best corrective action. File excerpts: 1. The CFO was reliable last year, so contrary evidence was disregarded. 2. The team has promised investors that the company will never fail. 3. A senior selected only documents supporting the original reserve. 4. The CEO can override normal journal approval. Required approach: Base the audit on sufficient appropriate evidence, maintain a questioning mind, distinguish audit assurance from investment guarantees, and address management override. Required: Identify the bias in the reserve testing.

choices.text: Sampling precision
Confirmation bias
A financial statement assertion
An independence safeguard

questions.explanation: The senior sought only evidence consistent with the initial belief.

questions.prompt: Review four statements from the engagement file and identify the best corrective action. File excerpts: 1. The CFO was reliable last year, so contrary evidence was disregarded. 2. The team has promised investors that the company will never fail. 3. A senior selected only documents supporting the original reserve. 4. The CEO can override normal journal approval. Required approach: Base the audit on sufficient appropriate evidence, maintain a questioning mind, distinguish audit assurance from investment guarantees, and address management override. Required: Respond to the CEO’s unrestricted entries.

choices.text: Eliminate substantive testing
Rely only on ordinary approvals
Perform procedures addressing management override
Accept an oral assurance

questions.explanation: Ordinary controls do not eliminate management-override risk.

questions.prompt: Which engagement reports specified procedures and factual findings without an opinion or assurance conclusion?

choices.text: Financial-statement audit.
Financial-statement review.
Agreed-upon procedures.
An examination of an assertion.

questions.explanation: Agreed-upon procedures reports what was done and found. An audit or examination expresses reasonable assurance; a review expresses limited assurance.

questions.prompt: Management will not acknowledge responsibility for preparing the financial statements. What does this affect?

choices.text: Only the auditor’s choice of sample size.
Only the wording of an invoice.
Nothing if the company has a controller.
An essential precondition for accepting the audit.

questions.explanation: Management’s acknowledgment of its responsibilities is an engagement precondition and cannot be replaced by auditor preparation of the statements.

questions.prompt: Before contacting a predecessor auditor about a prospective audit client, the successor should ordinarily obtain what?

choices.text: The prospective client’s permission to communicate.
The stock exchange’s approval.
A signed unmodified opinion.
A guarantee that no disagreements occurred.

questions.explanation: Client authorization permits relevant predecessor communications. The successor uses the resulting information to assess acceptance.

questions.prompt: A client asks to change an audit to a review solely because missing records would cause a modified opinion. Which response is best?

choices.text: Accept because a review requires less evidence.
Do not accept the change as a way to avoid the audit reporting consequence.
Accept if the fee is unchanged.
Issue the audit opinion without mentioning the missing evidence.

questions.explanation: A change intended to bypass an audit limitation is not a reasonable justification for downgrading assurance.

questions.prompt: Which service ordinarily provides limited assurance on historical financial statements through inquiry and analytical procedures?

choices.text: A compilation.
A financial-statement preparation engagement.
A financial-statement review.
An agreed-upon procedures engagement.

questions.explanation: A review provides limited assurance. Preparation, compilation, and agreed-upon procedures do not provide this assurance conclusion.

questions.prompt: Which item belongs in a financial-statement audit engagement letter?

choices.text: A promise that all fraud will be detected.
A guarantee of an unmodified opinion.
A waiver of access to material supporting records.
Management and auditor responsibilities and the applicable reporting framework.

questions.explanation: Written terms clarify responsibilities and scope without guaranteeing an outcome or waiving required evidence.

questions.prompt: Classify the requested services and decide whether proposed acceptance terms are appropriate. Service requests: Client A wants an opinion with reasonable assurance on annual statements. Client B wants limited assurance on historical statements. Client C wants only findings from inventory-count procedures agreed by the parties. Client D will refuse all access to material debt agreements. Acceptance criteria: Assume no law requires accepting Client D. Management must acknowledge its financial-reporting responsibility and provide information and access necessary for the engagement. Required: Appropriate service for Client A.

choices.text: Audit
Compilation
Preparation
Agreed-upon procedures

questions.explanation: An audit provides reasonable assurance and an opinion.

choices.text: Promise an unmodified opinion
Accept without documenting it
Replace debt evidence with the fee agreement
Resolve the restriction before accepting

questions.explanation: A material pre-acceptance scope restriction undermines the engagement preconditions.

questions.prompt: Audit documentation should be understandable to which person?

choices.text: Only the original preparer.
Only the client’s CFO.
Only a securities lawyer who designed the audit plan.
An experienced auditor with no previous connection to the engagement.

questions.explanation: Documentation must permit an experienced auditor unfamiliar with the engagement to understand the work and conclusions.

questions.prompt: A control deficiency creates a reasonable possibility that a material misstatement will not be detected and corrected timely. No actual misstatement has been found. How is it evaluated?

choices.text: It can be a material weakness despite the absence of an observed misstatement.
It cannot exceed a trivial deficiency.
It is automatically a qualified opinion on the financial statements.
It is irrelevant until fraud occurs.

questions.explanation: The classification considers potential magnitude and likelihood. It does not require an actual misstatement and does not automatically determine the financial-statement opinion.

questions.prompt: A required engagement quality review identifies an unresolved significant judgment before the report date. What should the partner do?

choices.text: Issue the report and resolve it next year.
Resolve the matter and complete the required review before report issuance.
Transfer all engagement responsibility to the reviewer.
Delete the reviewer’s comment.

questions.explanation: Required review procedures and differences of opinion must be addressed before issuance; responsibility is not transferred or avoided.

questions.prompt: Which statement best distinguishes a significant deficiency from a material weakness?

choices.text: A significant deficiency always requires a larger dollar error.
A material weakness exists only after fraud is proven.
A significant deficiency is less severe but important enough for governance attention.
The two labels have identical meanings.

questions.explanation: The distinction is based on severity and potential misstatement. Governance attention can be warranted below material-weakness severity.

questions.prompt: A team has contradictory evidence about an accounting estimate. What should the file document?

choices.text: Only the evidence supporting management.
Only an oral assurance from the partner.
A statement that contrary evidence was unnecessary.
The inconsistency, follow-up work, and basis for the conclusion.

questions.explanation: A defensible file shows how contradictory evidence was resolved and why the conclusion is supported.

questions.prompt: An auditor orally discusses a material weakness with the CFO. A written communication is required by the applicable standard. What remains necessary?

choices.text: Prepare and deliver the required written communication to the appropriate recipients.
Nothing, because oral communication always suffices.
Publish client details on a public website.
Wait until the weakness causes a loss.

questions.explanation: Required written communication remains necessary despite useful oral discussions. Confidentiality and timeliness still apply.

questions.prompt: Complete a reviewer’s action matrix for a nonissuer audit. Review findings: A: A material estimate conclusion has no documented reasoning. B: A control failure could permit a material misstatement with a reasonable possibility. C: A required written governance communication was only discussed orally. D: A required quality review remains unfinished on the planned issuance date. Scope: Assume the applicable standards require the written communication and engagement quality review described. Evaluate required actions rather than legal liability or a future damages claim. Required: Action for finding A.

choices.text: Rely only on memory
Document procedures, evidence, and the significant judgment
Delete the estimate from the file
Treat the checklist as conclusive

questions.explanation: The file must support significant judgments and conclusions.

questions.prompt: Complete a reviewer’s action matrix for a nonissuer audit. Review findings: A: A material estimate conclusion has no documented reasoning. B: A control failure could permit a material misstatement with a reasonable possibility. C: A required written governance communication was only discussed orally. D: A required quality review remains unfinished on the planned issuance date. Scope: Assume the applicable standards require the written communication and engagement quality review described. Evaluate required actions rather than legal liability or a future damages claim. Required: Classification considered for finding B.

choices.text: Automatically trivial
Only a sampling error
Material weakness
No deficiency without an actual error

questions.explanation: A reasonable possibility of an undetected material misstatement meets the material-weakness concept.

questions.prompt: Complete a reviewer’s action matrix for a nonissuer audit. Review findings: A: A material estimate conclusion has no documented reasoning. B: A control failure could permit a material misstatement with a reasonable possibility. C: A required written governance communication was only discussed orally. Evaluate required actions rather than legal liability or a future damages claim. Required: Action for finding C.

choices.text: Treat all oral discussion as sufficient
Communicate only next year
Disclose publicly instead
Complete the required written communication

questions.explanation: Oral discussion does not replace a required written communication.

questions.prompt: Complete a reviewer’s action matrix for a nonissuer audit. Review findings: A: A material estimate conclusion has no documented reasoning. B: A control failure could permit a material misstatement with a reasonable possibility. C: A required written governance communication was only discussed orally. D: A required quality review remains unfinished on the planned issuance date. Scope: Assume the applicable standards require the written communication and engagement quality review described. Evaluate required actions rather than legal liability or a future damages claim. Required: Action for finding D.

choices.text: Finish required review and resolve issues before issuance
Issue now and review later
Assign the opinion to the client
Omit the review from documentation

questions.explanation: Required quality procedures must precede issuance.
